answers.rationale: Inline diffs are essential for me to trust autonomous edits. I'd definitely use this feature if I can see exactly what changed before accepting. The review step removes my biggest friction point with code automation.

Checkpoint rollback is a game-changer. Knowing I can undo changes instantly if something goes wrong makes me way more willing to let an agent handle complex refactoring or multi-file updates. It's the safety net I need.
My biggest worry is that the agent makes subtle logic errors or breaks edge cases I don't catch in the diff review. Even well-intentioned changes can introduce bugs that don't show up immediately.

answers.value: Refactoring variable names and formatting in isolated utility functions with strong test coverage
answers.rationale: I'd start with low-risk refactoring tasks where the logic doesn't change and I have good tests. Variable renames and formatting are mechanical, easy to review, and the impact is contained. Perfect way to build trust before moving to riskier tasks.
